This simple habit is linked to a 33% lower risk of Alzheimer's

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Reading for enjoyment may offer far more than entertainment. Whether someone prefers a classic Jane Austen novel or a Heartstopper graphic novel, research suggests that reading for pleasure is associated with better mental health, stronger empathy, and a lower risk of dementia.

Researchers at the University of Cambridge are working with The Queen's Reading Room, a charity established by Her Majesty The Queen, to raise awareness of these benefits across all age groups. Their collaboration is part of the National Year of Reading, an initiative encouraging more people to make reading part of their lives.

Recent findings suggest that cambridge psychiatry researchers Professor Barbara Sahakian and Dr. Christelle Langley began exploring the subject while writing their 2025 book, Brain Boost: Healthy Habits for a Happier Life. They discovered that reading for enjoyment was connected to a remarkably wide range of positive outcomes, yet the amount of research specifically examining these benefits was surprisingly limited.

Recent findings suggest that in a review published in Psychological Medicine, Sahakian and Langley joined Vicki Perrin, CEO of The Queen's Reading Room, to examine the available evidence. Their findings suggest that the format and type of reading matter less than the enjoyment people get from it. They also highlight how reading together, whether through book clubs or parents sharing stories with children, can provide additional benefits.

Industry observers note that professor Sahakian said: "Reading is a great way to support our brain health, develop notable cognitive skills and boost our well-being. It's something we ought to be encouraging from an early age, given the increasing evidence of its benefits, particularly to children, but really, it's never too late to start, and it can bring benefits throughout our lives and into old age.".

Reading Early in Life Is Linked to Better Brain Development.

Despite the growing evidence of its advantages, reading for enjoyment has become less common among young people. Surveys indicate that reading rates among children and teenagers have fallen to their lowest recorded levels, with particularly steep challenges among teenage boys and children from disadvantaged backgrounds.

Even children who are least enthusiastic about reading recognize that it can help them academically. Nearly half acknowledge that books and other reading materials can introduce them to unfamiliar words or teach them something new.

One of the most compelling studies examined more than 10,000 young people. Conducted by Sahakian, Langley, and their colleagues, the research found that children who started reading for pleasure at an early age tended to perform better in several crucial areas. These included attention, memory, and executive functioning, the mental abilities involved in planning, decision-making, and managing behavior.

Sources indicate that early readers also showed stronger academic performance, experienced fewer mental health problems, and were more likely to develop healthier daily routines. In particular, they tended to get more sleep and spend less time using screens.

In a recent development, dr. Langley said: "Given how beneficial reading for pleasure is at a young age, we should be doing everything we can to introduce children and young people to reading. The important thing is to find something they'd really enjoy reading about - it might be a TV program or a game - and use this as a way in. Reading comics and graphic novels could also be a helpful introduction as they might be seen as less intimidating, maybe less boring, than novels.".

Recent findings suggest that the academic advantages may extend beyond language and literacy. Studies have also connected reading with stronger mathematical performance. Researchers suggest this relationship may arise because both activities rely on some of the same mental abilities, including language processing, memory, and executive function.

Just Five Minutes of Reading May Reduce Stress.

The benefits of reading do not disappear after childhood. Among adults, surveys have associated reading for enjoyment with improved emotional well-being, greater relaxation, and reduced stress. Readers also tend to report more empathy, a deeper understanding of other people, and greater openness to viewpoints different from their own.

In a recent development, for many people, books are an especially appealing way to unwind. Reading ranks as the most popular approach to stress relief, with nearly two in five adults (38%) identifying it as their preferred way to relax.

A neuroscience study commissioned by The Queen's Reading Room in 2024 found that spending just five minutes reading fiction could lower stress by as much as 20%. The study also reported improvements in concentration and problem-solving abilities, along with a reduced sense of loneliness.

Books may even provide more comfort than some traditional relaxation habits. In one survey, more respondents stated they turned to reading (35%) for comfort than to drinking wine (31%) or taking a hot bath (10%).

Reading Linked to Lower Dementia and Alzheimer's Risk.

Recent findings suggest that as people get older, the potential advantages of reading may become especially meaningful. Research has associated mentally stimulating leisure activities, including reading, with slower cognitive decline and a reduced likelihood of developing dementia.

Industry observers note that one study followed nearly 5,500 adults aged 55 and older for five years. Participants who regularly took part in activities such as reading were significantly less likely to develop cognitive impairment during the study period.

Recent findings suggest that another investigation reported an even more striking association. People who read newspapers, magazines, and books had a 33% lower risk of Alzheimer's disease.

Sources indicate that these findings suggest that keeping the mind engaged through reading may support cognitive health in later life. However, the researchers emphasize that most of the available studies identify associations rather than proving that reading itself prevents dementia.

How Reading May Change the Structure of the Brain.

Sources indicate that what could explain the many benefits associated with reading? Brain imaging research offers some intriguing clues.

Studies have identified differences in brain structure associated with reading, particularly in regions responsible for language, learning, emotional regulation, and executive control. These differences include greater brain volume and larger cortical areas in certain regions, as well as thicker cortex in areas key for language processing.

Researchers have also observed stronger connections within the brain's white matter, which helps different regions communicate and supports the processing of language.

Although much of this evidence is correlational, some research suggests that reading-related training can directly influence the brain's physical structure.

Sources indicate that in one small study involving 11 children with dyslexia between the ages of 7 and 11, researchers tested an eight-week training program designed to strengthen reading abilities. The exercises involved mental imagery, articulation, and tracing letters, combinations of letters, and words.

Industry observers note that following the program, the children demonstrated significant improvements in reading skills. Brain scans also revealed increases in gray matter volume in key regions, providing evidence that reading interventions can be accompanied by measurable structural changes in the brain.

Why Reading Together May Offer Even Greater Benefits.

According to recent reports, reading does not have to be a solitary activity. Researchers suggest that sharing books with other people can add a valuable social dimension, creating opportunities for connection and potentially improving both mental and physical well-being.

According to recent reports, the Queen's Reading Room has made this idea a central part of its mission. Released on social media in January 2021, the initiative originally provided a way for people to exchange book recommendations and stay connected during pandemic lockdowns.

It has since expanded into an international community reaching more than 12 million people across 184 countries. Through its flagship festival, neuroscience research, and other programs, the charity works to make reading a more prominent part of everyday life.

Its activities also extend to homeless shelters and domestic violence refuges, where shared reading is used as a therapeutic resource to help people during recovery.

The social connections created through reading groups may be particularly valuable for older adults, who can face increased isolation and reduced opportunities to participate in physically demanding activities.

Sources indicate that professor Sahakian noted: "Shared reading groups and book clubs appear to provide additional benefits through social interaction. They can help people feel less isolated and more connected to others, which has been shown to reduce the risk of dementia.

"While these clubs can be fun and beneficial at any age, they're perfect for older people who may not be so mobile - they might not be able to go out as an exercise group or a cycling group, but a reading group is something most people can enjoy.".

It has been revealed that the researchers' overall message is that people can benefit from reading at any stage of life. Whether someone enjoys novels, newspapers, comics, or stories shared with friends, making time for reading may help support cognitive health, emotional well-being, and social connection.

Vicki Perrin, CEO of The Queen's Reading Room, added: "At The Queen's Reading Room, we have seen first-hand the transformative power of individual and shared reading to change lives. Books truly do make life better, and we're excited to do our bit to help everyone, everywhere, make more room for reading.".

Materials provided by University of Cambridge. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

Fewer choices available to enrollees on ACA exchanges: RWJF" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

The number of regions where patients have limited choices for Affordable Care Act intends is on the rise, according to a newly introduced analysis.

The Robert Wood Johnson Foundation report found that for the 2027 plan year, there are more than 200 counties in which there is only one insurer available, and close to 1,000 where there are just two intends available for consumers to choose from.

This makes for an increase of 50% from the 2026 strategy year, with more than a third of counties having limited options on the ACA's marketplaces for 2027.

In a recent development, most states (39) will have at least one county where plan choices are limited for enrollees. For about half of these states, this is the norm and aligns with 2026, but for the rest, this marks a significant shift, the RWJF researchers wrote in the report.

"For the individual market as a whole, the decline in participation is sobering but not a fatal blow," per the report. "The presence of federal and some state subsidies provides an important backstop that will likely prevent a complete meltdown.".

"Yet the prospect of a growing number of counties with little insurer participation is grim, and likely will not bode well for premium increases, morbidity or enrollment going forward," according to the report.

Recent findings suggest that the foundation cites a recent analysis from Wakely that found the individual market declined by 16% in the first six months of 2026. The end of the enhanced premium tax credits, cost pressures and growing administrative burdens are likely to contribute to worsening trends in this space.

For instance, ACA marketplace exits from Cigna, CareSource and Medica are having a significant impact in Iowa and Indiana for the coming proposal year, the researchers found. In the latter case, most Indiana counties have two or fewer plan choices.

In a recent development, however, there are some bright spots, RWJF researchers wrote. There are certain insurers participating in the exchanges who have beefed up their footprints, and there is a smattering of new entrants. Oscar Health, for example, is planning the largest growth, entering a new state and adding new counties in some of the states it already serves.

Some insurers, like Centene and UnitedHealthcare, are making strategic exits in some markets while entering others, for a neutral impact on their footprints overall.

Insurers like Antidote Health and Peak Health are also entering new regions—even if on a limited basis in some cases—which can help staunch the bleeding.

Blue Cross Blue Shield plans also often play a key role in limited markets, as in close to 80% of counties with a single insurer, that payer is a Blues plan. In addition, in 12% of counties, the single insurer is Elevance Health, which operates plans as Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield.

Recent findings suggest that "This suggests that were it not for the somewhat unique role of Blues plans as a backstop, the threat of a bare county might be higher," per the report. "Single-state Blues, in particular, are under social and political pressure to participate in much if not all of their state, and do not feel as free to exit unprofitable counties as are publicly traded insurers.".

Key insights from HPE’s Q4 earnings report

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1619 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co.delivered a record fiscal fourth quarter this week, roughly doubling its fiscal 2027 growth outlook, but its stock gave back nearly all of the prior day’s rally.
  • Fourth-quarter revenue rose 50%, to $14.5 billion, orders grew 88%, and adjusted earnings of $1.43 per share topped the high end of guidance.
  • Recent findings suggest that I joined a briefing with Chief Executive Antonio Neri and a small group of independent analysts shortly before the results came out.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 15:27 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

ANALYSIS by Zeus Kerravala.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co.delivered a record fiscal fourth quarter this week, roughly doubling its fiscal 2027 growth outlook, but its stock gave back nearly all of the prior day’s rally. The selloff suggests Wall Street still prices HPE as a low-margin server vendor, even though the results describe a networking and artificial intelligence infrastructure company with demand exceeding its ability to ship.

Fourth-quarter revenue rose 50%, to $14.5 billion, orders grew 88%, and adjusted earnings of $1.43 per share topped the high end of guidance. HPE now expects fiscal 2027 revenue to grow 27% to 35%, with adjusted earnings of $5.05 to $5.35 per share, according to its earnings release.

Recent findings suggest that I joined a briefing with Chief Executive Antonio Neri and a small group of independent analysts shortly before the results came out. Here are my four takeaways for investors and information technology leaders:.

Neri explained that networking orders grew more than 4.5 times faster than networking revenue in the quarter, up from 3.5 times the quarter before, and HPE exited the year with $10.5 billion in AI backlog.

HPE doubled its networking purchase commitments over the summer and raised them again in the fourth quarter, but those components carry lead times of 28 to 40-plus weeks, so Neri expects networking conversion to pick up starting in the second quarter. Supply constraints are a better problem to have than weak demand, but they mean fiscal 2027 hinges on converting orders rather than winning them.

The Juniper Networks integration is complete, and the annual cost-synergy target has risen to $800 million, but the bigger story remains the profit mix. Chief Financial Officer Marie Myers said networking will account for more than 40% of HPE’s operating profit by the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027, up from less than a quarter of revenue. AI is a major driver, with routing orders growing by triple digits as customers connect AI data centers to one another.

Security was the soft spot, which Neri called “just timing.” When I asked whether the security portfolio is where he wants it as the industry consolidates around significant platforms, he argued for a different path.

Sources indicate that “Fortinet and we have a different strategy — the convergence of security and networking — and we are taking it all the way down to the silicon level,” he stated. The convergence of networking and security is underway but will take time to execute, as a considerable amount of technical debt must go through its depreciation cycle. In a greenfield situation, organizations can easily deploy a converged solution, but in a brownfield environment, it requires much more work. This is the right strategy, but it remains a “prove-it” business for HPE.

Industry observers note that many neoclouds rely on vendor financing and chip-backed debt, raising real concerns about who is left exposed if the buildout slows. HPE indicates it has stayed out, and Neri was quite emphatic about it on the briefing.

“I want to be clear: We have not financed any neocloud through HPFS, our financing arm,” he mentioned. “We have zero exposure to any AI financing for neocloud.” HPE has likely left some revenue on the table, but it drew the line in the right place. It will sell to neoclouds, as its $1.2 billion Vultr order shows, without acting as their bank. Enterprise and sovereign customers account for the majority of its cumulative AI orders, and if the neocloud financing chain breaks, HPE’s financing arm won’t be the one holding the paper.

According to recent reports, training built the first phase of AI infrastructure, and Neri believes inference will build the next and will dominate demand for AI infrastructure. “I believe by the end of the decade, 80% will be in AI inferencing,” he noted. “Much of that will land on-prem. Much of that will be distributed, for sure. That’s why the server business is structurally well-positioned.”.

In a recent development, once agents are in production, token costs become a recurring bill, and companies will want inference running alongside their own data. Those servers require far more memory and pull in storage and services, which is better business than racking graphics processing units for a hyperscaler.

Evidence of this is the interest in Helios, the Advanced Microdevices Inc. rack that uses HPE’s Ethernet switching rather than Nvidia’s proprietary interconnect. I asked Neri whether Jensen Huang’s brief departure from Nvidia Corp. had opened that door. He remarked interest was building before then, as customers look to diversify.

Recent findings suggest that HPE shares jumped 17% on Monday ahead of the report as part of a broader AI rally, then fell about 13% in early trading on Tuesday, ending near where they started the week. I see three reasons for this.

The first is margins. Cloud & AI operating margin was 18.4% in the quarter, and HPE guided to about 14% for fiscal 2027. Reuters reported that JPMorgan analysts called margin mix the key debate for investors.

Industry observers note that the second is pricing. Myers noted higher selling prices have been the biggest driver of server growth, and she expects gross margin to moderate in the second half as AI server volumes ramp and costs rise faster than pricing.

The third is timing. HPE expects about 54% of revenue in the second half, with the ramp tied to Helios shipments, the Oracle Corp. deal, customer data center readiness and component supply. Those are fair execution questions, but they miss the shift in where HPE’s profit comes from.

In a recent development, on the topic of margins, the 18.4% came off an unusual stretch of favorable pricing that should not have been modeled as permanent. Neri argued the guide is still “significantly higher than any historical margin we have had in this business,” and he’s right outside the past year. A year ago, the segment’s margin was 9.3%. Margin rate also isn’t margin dollars. At 30% to 40% revenue growth, my math highlights Cloud & AI adding well over $1 billion in operating profit at the midpoint.

It has been revealed that the bears are right that price-driven server growth doesn’t warrant a premium multiple, which is why the mix matters more. The market is fixated on the segment whose margins are normalizing and ignoring the one whose margins are expanding. Adjusted earnings per share are still guided to grow by 27% to 35%, in line with revenue growth. That’s far from the margin doom-and-gloom narrative on the stock.

Recent findings suggest that the back-half concern is real but manageable. Myers described the pipeline as multiples of the backlog, and Neri noted the guide assumes only historical win rates against it.

Then there’s quality. HPE is guiding to about 30% growth and at least $5.5 billion in free cash flow, has no neocloud financing exposure and has already brought leverage below its target. It trades at about eight times the midpoint of its adjusted earnings guidance. “I don’t see us at a multiple that is 8 to 9x; it makes no sense whatsoever,” Neri mentioned on the earnings call.

Sources indicate that for old HPE, that’s true, as it’s a server vendor, but HPE is increasingly a network vendor each quarter. In fact, during our pre-call with Neri, he led with networking and spoke at length about the business before pivoting to the server business. Expect networking to continue to drive a larger share of profits.

In a recent development, fiscal 2027 is an execution year. HPE must convert purchase commitments into shipments, ramp Helios and prove that networking margins can climb even as cloud and AI margins settle. I’ll be watching networking order conversion more closely than server margins. If HPE executes, today’s multiple will prove to be too low.

Industry observers note that zeus Kerravala is a principal analyst at ZK Research, a division of Kerravala Consulting. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE.

#169344. Scientists discover a hidden eye disease that slowly steals night vision

Scientists discover a hidden eye disease that slowly steals night vision

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1044 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A newly identified genetic eye disease can gradually interfere with night vision and the ability to see objects at the edges of the visual field.
  • Recent findings suggest that an international research team, including scientists at the Scheie Eye Institute within the University of Pennsylvania's Perelman School of Medicine, traced the condition to a gene already associated with another form of vision loss.
  • In a recent development, although the condition has not yet received an official name, researchers are calling it EFEMP1-associated late-onset retinal degeneration (L-ORD).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A newly identified genetic eye disease can gradually interfere with night vision and the ability to see objects at the edges of the visual field. The condition may be especially difficult to recognize because people can maintain good eyesight for much of their lives before noticeable problems develop.

Recent findings suggest that an international research team, including scientists at the Scheie Eye Institute within the University of Pennsylvania's Perelman School of Medicine, traced the condition to a gene already associated with another form of vision loss. However, the two diseases affect eyesight in strikingly different ways. The previously known disorder primarily damages central vision, while the newly discovered condition affects peripheral vision and the ability to see in darkness.

In a recent development, although the condition has not yet received an official name, researchers are calling it EFEMP1-associated late-onset retinal degeneration (L-ORD). It is linked to a specific genetic variant known as p.Arg140Trp in the EFEMP1 gene. This change causes an unusually thick accumulation of material between cells in the eye.

A Genetic Discovery That Began Decades Ago.

The investigation traces back to 1998, when doctors documented an unusual pattern of vision loss in a family in the United States. As researchers uncovered new genetic evidence, they were able to connect those findings to families in Europe who indicated similar symptoms.

Industry observers note that the study, published in JAMA Ophthalmology, examined three unrelated families from different countries who carried the p.Arg140Trp variant. Their symptoms were compared with those of another family carrying a different change in the same gene, called p.Arg345Trp, which is associated with the previously recognized disease affecting central vision.

The international collaboration included researchers from Penn Medicine, the University of Edinburgh, the University of Basel, Charles University, and the University of Bonn.

At first, scientists suspected that the unusual symptoms in the original family might be caused by a different genetic disorder. Testing, however, failed to identify the variants responsible for that condition.

"The different disease expression in this family was thought to be similar to a condition caused by C1QTNF5 gene variants. However, none of the variants associated with that disease were found," stated Artur V. Cideciyan, PhD, an ophthalmology researcher and co-director of the Center for Hereditary Retinal Degenerations. "Our collaborators then discovered a upcoming variant in the EFEMP1 gene that normally causes a different disease where the macula, which is tied to central vision, is affected first.".

How the Upcoming Eye Disease Affects Night Vision.

Industry observers note that the researchers found that the newly identified condition develops gradually in the outer regions of the retina. Located at the back of the eye, the retina detects incoming light and transforms it into signals that the brain uses to create visual images.

In a recent development, unlike the previously known EFEMP1 disorder, which initially affects the macula and central vision, this newly identified disease begins in the peripheral retina. People may see normally for much of their lives before gradually noticing that their side vision is narrowing or that seeing in dim surroundings has become more difficult.

Problems may be particularly noticeable around dusk or at night, when the eyes must rely more heavily on specialized light-sensitive cells called rods.

One reason the disease is challenging to diagnose is that these cells may initially show no visible structural damage. The gradual progression of symptoms can make the condition even harder to recognize.

According to recent reports, however, the researchers identified a potentially valuable early clue. In affected individuals, rod cells take unusually long to recover when the eyes move from bright surroundings into darkness. This abnormal response can be detected even when the retina still appears structurally normal.

Industry observers note that "We can detect a major abnormality in the way rod photoreceptors recover in darkness with retinas that still look structurally intact," Cideciyan mentioned. "This gives us a functional marker of disease at a stage when photoreceptor cells have not yet been lost.".

The finding suggests that changes in how the retina functions may reveal the disease before the light-sensitive cells responsible for vision begin to disappear.

What the Discovery Could Mean for Age-Related Vision Loss.

An important question remains unanswered: How many people carry this newly identified genetic variant?

Recent findings suggest that researchers suspect the condition is relatively uncommon, but they do not yet have enough information to determine its prevalence. Larger investigations will be necessary to establish how frequently the variant occurs and how many people may be affected.

According to recent reports, beyond identifying another inherited eye disorder, the findings could help scientists better understand why vision deteriorates with age. Studying rare genetic diseases can reveal biological processes that may also contribute to much more widespread retinal conditions.

Sources indicate that "Aging is a risk factor for many medical conditions, including retinal diseases such as age-related macular degeneration, the most common retinal condition of aging," remarked Tomas S. Aleman, MD, a professor of ophthalmology and the other co-director of the Center for Hereditary Retinal Degenerations. "Lessons learned from these infrequent, late-onset genetic eye diseases offer glimpses at possible mechanisms of disease for much more frequent retinal problems.".

Industry observers note that by revealing how different changes in a single gene can produce distinct patterns of vision loss, the research adds to scientists' understanding of inherited retinal disease. It also highlights the potential importance of detecting changes in visual function before damage becomes apparent in the retina's structure.

In a recent development, the study received support from the University of Edinburgh Chancellor's Fellowship award, RS Macdonald Charitable Trust Seedcorn Award, the BrightFocus Foundation (M2024009N), the German Research Foundation (532367710), the Medical Research Council (MC_UU_00035/9, MC_UU_00007/10), the Swiss National Science Foundation (204285), the Ministry of Health of the Czech Republic (NW24-06-00083), Charles University in Prague (UNCE/24/MED/022 and SVV 2600631), and the Samuel G. Jacobson, MD, PhD, Memorial Fund.

Sources indicate that materials provided by University of Pennsylvania School of Medicine. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes
Catching up with the new CEO of UnitedHealthcare's Surest" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

Joe Clark is stepping into the CEO chair at UnitedHealthcare's Surest unit with an eye on affordability.

In a recent development, clark was appointed to lead the division earlier this month, after serving as the chief financial officer for the insurer's employer and individual segment. In an interview with Fierce Healthcare, he mentioned that the new role comes at "an exciting time" to be a part of a proposal like Surest.

Sources indicate that under the model, Surest eliminates deductibles for a copayment-only approach, where members' costs are tied to the quality and value for their provider. Members connect to the Surest app or website to compare the cost between different providers.

According to recent reports, "Affordability is a challenge every year, but especially right now, for employers," Clark noted. "We've seen demand for Surest and other sort of alternative health looks just skyrocket over the last year. And being part of being able to deliver that and offer solutions to employers is incredibly exciting.".

UnitedHealthcare first rolled out the unit in 2016 as Bind before rebranding as Surest in 2022 with an eye on growth. In a 2023 report, the company mentioned that Surest members had 6% fewer emergency department visits and 13% fewer inpatient admissions compared to people enrolled in traditional commercial plans at the same company.

The strategy also saw a 20% increase in visits to a physician and 9% increase in preventative physical exams compared to the members in traditional prepares.

In a recent development, in a 2024 analysis, conducted by Aon, the company found that Surest enrollees generated $400 or more in cost claims savings per year. That study also identified improvements around spending and utilization across all age groups and accounting for several conditions.

Clark remarked that in a traditional health plan, only about 15% of people hit their deductible for the year, meaning they're ultimately not using their insurance during that time frame. Surest removes that problem by eliminating the deductible and puts the power in the consumers' hands to make choices for their own care.

He added that the Net Promoter Score for Surest is higher than its other commercial strategy offerings. Consumers report satisfaction with the digital experience and the cost certainty that the plan presents, Clark noted.

"It's very much like the Amazon shopping experience, but for healthcare, which hasn't happened before," Clark remarked.

Surest also aims to personalize the member experience by leaning on AI and other digital tools to present data on providers and costs that may be of use to the user, while leaving the ultimate decision in their hands.

Sources indicate that "The consumer is in charge with their doctor in making those decisions," Clark said. "But we want to make sure that we are giving you, similar to what you would see with any shopping app, a personalized recommendation of what is a good fit.".

Clark said that starting his career on the actuarial side of healthcare made plain how much of a challenge affordability can be, and that drew him to pursue his current path. Prior to UnitedHealthcare, he served as an associate partner at McKinsey and as an actuary at Cigna.

Through Surest, he believes he can help lead the charge toward a more modern healthcare system, he said.

In a recent development, as for the future of Surest, the first piece is continuing to make sure the team delivers on a personalized and simple-to-understand experience for consumers. The next level is building on that consumer-focused experience to add a provider layer, and work with them on the quality and value scores that are surfaced to members.

It has been revealed that for example, a provider may consistently recommend a patient seek an MRI scan at a hospital rather than at a lower-cost lab. And Surest is gaining the "critical mass" of members where providers actively want to have these conversations, Clark noted.

"I see that as sort of the next evolution beyond working with consumers and members: moving to providers as well," he remarked.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 16:12 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Lawmakers on both sides of the aisle are criticizing Nvidia Corp.’s decision to rehire Jensen Huang as its chief executive.

The criticism came against the backdrop of a controversial move by the U.S. Commerce Department. The agency applied fresh export restrictions to Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud operator. The organization played a prominent role in the spy controversy that led to Huang’s resignation. According to trade experts, the Commerce Department left out a key clause that is usually included in such restrictions.

Huang resigned on Nov. 12 following revelations that he had an affair with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive. Early reporting about the relationship indicated that she was found to have passed intelligence to China. The U.S. Justice Department later stated that it has not yet reached a conclusion on whether Alice Huang is a spy. Earlier this week, the Upcoming York Times reported that she maintained contact with a Chinese intelligence official.

In a recent development, nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang on Monday after U.S. President Donald Trump and tech industry figures urged directors to bring him back. The move drew widespread criticism from members of Congress.

Recent findings suggest that house Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-Latest York), who is set to become House Speaker, called the reinstatement “indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible.” Rep. Don Bacon (R-Nebraska), the chair of House Subcommittee on Cyber, Information Technologies and Innovation, said that “it’s inexplicable to me why they want this guy back as CEO.” Former Utah Republican Senator and Massachusetts Governor Mitt Romney tweeted: “Let me get this straight: we rushed AI along without regulating safeguards in order to stay ahead of China and at the same time, we sold China the very chips they’d need to get ahead of us. Smells of profit, corruption and perhaps worse.”.

In a recent development, multiple lawmakers told CNBC that they proposal to scrutinize Huang’s conduct closely. The executive is scheduled to testify before multiple Congressional committees next Tuesday. Furthermore, Sen. Ron Wyden (D-Oregon) told the outlet that Democrats plan to scrutinize the Trump administration’s role in the matter.

Recent findings suggest that the Commerce Department today added Megaspeed and several of its regional affiliates to its Entity List. Companies on the list can only purchase sensitive products such as graphics cards if they obtain a license from the U.S. government. According to Gizmodo, the move has drawn scrutiny because the restrictions applied to Megaspeed include a loophole.

All the companies on the Entity List are prohibited from buying Nvidia’s latest chips unless they secure a license. Most of them are also unable to buy lower-end graphics cards, high-bandwidth memory and related hardware. The latter restrictions are specified in a clause called the FDPR provision. The Commerce Department has reportedly not applied the FDPR provision to Megaspeed when it added the company to the Entity List.

Recent findings suggest that huang returned to Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters on Monday. The news sent the chipmaker’s stock soaring more than 30%, although it parred some of the gains today. Nvidia shares are down 5.8% from Monday.

Wired today published excerpts from Huang’s all-hands meeting with employees. The executive apologized for his affairs and for his management style, which has also come under scrutiny in recent days. He added that he will undergo a “360-degree review” and that Nvidia’s code of conduct is still in effect.

A common blood pressure drug has a surprising effect on calorie-burning brown fat

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1180 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A widely used blood pressure medication may have an unexpected benefit beyond its ability to control hypertension.
  • Sources indicate that losartan belongs to a class of medications called angiotensin receptor blockers (ARB), which have an established safety profile.
  • The findings also revealed a surprising connection between brown fat and mental health.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A widely used blood pressure medication may have an unexpected benefit beyond its ability to control hypertension. Scientists have found that losartan can activate brown fat, a specialized type of body fat that burns energy, and improve metabolic activity in mice. The discovery suggests that an existing medication could potentially be repurposed to stimulate brown fat and support metabolic health.

Sources indicate that losartan belongs to a class of medications called angiotensin receptor blockers (ARB), which have an established safety profile. In a new study published in Nature, researchers found that the drug increased brown fat activity through a biological mechanism separate from its blood pressure effects. This raises the possibility of developing treatments that activate brown fat without lowering blood pressure.

The findings also revealed a surprising connection between brown fat and mental health. After examining data from more than 100,000 patients, researchers discovered that people with detectable brown fat had lower rates of several medical conditions, including anxiety and depression. This is the first time the research team has reported associations between brown fat and psychiatric health, adding to earlier evidence linking the tissue to better cardiovascular and metabolic health.

According to recent reports, the research was led by Paul Cohen at Rockefeller University's Laboratory of Molecular Metabolism, working with Heiko Schöder and Daniel Lafontaine from Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSKCC). It expands on research published in 2021, when Cohen's team analyzed approximately 50,000 patients and found that those with more brown fat had substantially lower odds of developing cardiometabolic conditions such as coronary artery disease and type II diabetes.

According to recent reports, "We only looked for a few diagnostic codes in that study, mainly focusing on cardiovascular disease since that's what this tissue has historically been associated with," says Cohen. "The scope of this new analysis is far more expansive. We doubled our number of patients and considered more than 500 codes, which allowed us to unearth many new insights.".

AI Analysis Reveals New Benefits of Brown Fat.

According to recent reports, to investigate brown fat's relationship with human health, the researchers examined PET/CT scans from more than 100,000 patients who had undergone imaging as part of their cancer monitoring. They focused on scans showing brown adipose tissue, which can be found in six regions of the body, including the neck, armpits, and areas around organs such as the heart and kidneys.

Recent findings suggest that the team used an approach known as reverse translation, which begins with observations in patients and then investigates the biological processes responsible for them. Cohen's laboratory has previously used this strategy to uncover crucial details about brown fat and its effects on health.

Nicolás Gómez-Banoy, the study's first author and an endocrinologist and instructor in clinical investigation in Cohen's laboratory, used a machine learning system developed by researchers at MSKCC to measure brown fat activity. The technology allowed him to assess both the total activity in each patient and the activity within each of the six anatomical regions.

Sources indicate that the analysis indicated that brown fat's location could be just as key as its presence. Activity in particular regions appeared to have stronger associations with certain health conditions, suggesting that brown fat may influence the body differently depending on where it is found.

"For example, the axillary, or armpit, area was linked to a decreased risk of high blood pressure compared to other regions," he claims. "But overall, patients with brown fat have better glycemic parameters, lipid profiles, and echocardiographic indices, as well as lower inflammatory markers.".

These findings indicate that people with brown fat tend to have healthier blood sugar levels, blood fat profiles, measures of heart function, and indicators of inflammation.

Common Blood Pressure Drug Activates Brown Fat.

It has been revealed that as the researchers investigated medications associated with brown fat activity, they noticed an intriguing pattern. Patients taking angiotensin receptor blockers were more likely to have detectable brown fat on their scans, suggesting that these widely prescribed medications might influence the tissue.

To explore that possibility, the team conducted laboratory experiments using cultured brown fat cells. They found that losartan directly increased the cells' metabolic activity, providing evidence that the drug could stimulate brown fat rather than simply being associated with its presence.

Even more interestingly, the researchers discovered that losartan activated brown fat through molecular pathways different from those responsible for lowering blood pressure. That distinction could be especially valuable for developing future medications that target metabolism without interfering with normal blood pressure regulation.

Recent findings suggest that "The fact that its different effects are mediated by different molecular pathways is advantageous, since it means we could potentially isolate them in future therapies," says Gómez-Banoy. "That way you would be able to stimulate brown fat in people with normal blood pressure.".

According to recent reports, additional experiments in healthy mice strengthened the findings. Animals given losartan showed increased energy expenditure, consumed more oxygen, and produced more carbon dioxide, all signs of heightened metabolic activity. Despite these changes, their body weight remained stable.

Brown Fat's Surprising Connection to Mental Health.

According to recent reports, beyond its metabolic effects, brown fat may have a previously unrecognized relationship with psychological well-being. The patient analysis revealed that individuals with detectable brown fat had lower rates of anxiety and depression, extending the tissue's potential health associations beyond the cardiovascular system.

"We know that metabolically healthy people tend to have lower incidence of psychiatric diseases, so it could be that having brown fat makes you more metabolically healthy, and this correlates with fewer psychiatric challenges," claims Gómez-Banoy.

The researchers also found an intriguing relationship involving selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, or SSRIs, medications commonly prescribed to treat depression. These drugs appeared to suppress brown fat activity, suggesting another possible connection between psychiatric treatments and metabolic regulation.

According to recent reports, however, the findings do not suggest that brown fat is beneficial in every respect. The analysis also identified higher rates of osteoporosis and certain skin diseases among people with brown fat, raising questions about possible trade-offs that require further investigation.

Industry observers note that the discoveries have opened several avenues for future research. Scientists hope to examine the genetics of people with particularly high brown fat activity, investigate why the tissue is associated with lower rates of anxiety and depression, and determine whether its apparent benefits can be harnessed safely.

Losartan may also be only one of several existing medications worth investigating. The extensive patient analysis identified additional drugs associated with brown fat activity, offering researchers a range of potential candidates for future studies.

"There were plenty of other medications associated with brown fat activity in our large cohort," Cohen notes. "This is just a start.".

Stay up to date on the latest in health tech, digital health and health AI news with this weekly brief. Read below for news from the week of Nov. 16 to 27.

Waystar said Tuesday it will integrate its AI-driven revenue cycle solutions into Google Cloud’s recently unveiled Gemini for healthcare solution.

According to recent reports, the integration reflects an expanded partnership between Waystar and Google Cloud. Through it, users will have increased access to Waystar AltitudeAI innovations, advanced analytics and revenue cycle insights.

“By bringing Waystar's AI-powered revenue cycle capabilities into Gemini for healthcare, we're helping providers simplify some of the most complex operational and financial tasks in care delivery,” said Aashima Gupta, Google Cloud managing director of healthcare, in a statement. “Together, we are unifying data and workflows in a secure, governed workspace that drives better outcomes across the healthcare ecosystem.”.

OpenAI is expanding ChatGPT’s health capabilities across various channels, it remarked Thursday.

The company’s Health feature is expanding to desktop app, Androids and its personal AI agents—dubbed dots.

Among the latest capabilities include:.

ChatGPT Health is currently available to Free, Go, Plus, and Pro users in the U.S., while dots are available to Pro users.

Oracle launched a new agentic experience for life science organizations to improve clinical trial operations.

Oracle Life Science AI Agents is currently available for early adopters with a focus on portfolio monitoring, trial planning and conduct. The company plans to expand into clinical development domains, including data management, post-trial analytics and trial design.

Agents are designed to work with human oversight, executives say.

Oracle Health and Life Sciences EVP and General Manager Seema Verma said in a statement clinical development requires companies to “coordinate complex operational activity.”.

“We are bringing AI-assisted intelligence into clinical trial operations to help organizations to monitor performance, identify emerging risks, and coordinate responses across the trial lifecycle,” Verma said. “By combining Oracle’s Life Sciences applications, AI-assisted capabilities, connected data services, on a secure, scalable cloud infrastructure, we are helping organizations coordinate clinical research workflows and operational decisions across their clinical trial environments.”.

Agentic company Artera announced the roll out of an intake solution using AI Agents to collect, check and complete information throughout the patient visit.

Artera Intake has three core workflows, executives say: pre-visit intake, in-office and walk-in intake and complex form and consent digitization. The workflows are housed in a latest Intake Hub, according to the Nov. 19 announcement.

Chief Product and Strategy Officer Zach Wood noted in a statement what differentiates the solution from others is “where it starts.”.

“Most intake solutions are built first, and providers have to change their workflows to fit them,” Wood said. “We start with the provider. We learn how their teams and patients actually move through intake, then build the agentic solution around that, together.”.

Wood continued, “That starting point shapes everything that follows, and is designed to drive faster adoption, more completed intake and real value for practices.”.

According to recent reports, amazon Connect Health unveiled Nov. 17 the launch of expanded patient access capabilities through the agentic solution.

As of the date of the announcement, four new capabilities are generally available to consumers: appointment management, prescription management, information assistance and password reset.

The firm states the expansion builds on the foundation of Amazon Connect Health, which included patient verification, patient insights, ambient documentation and more.

One health system using the tool is Philadelphia-based Temple Health. AVP of Patient Access Joseph Alfonsi said in a statement the tool has handled patient verification on thousands of calls weekly since the system went live in June.

Sources indicate that “Building on that success, we’re excited to expand agentic patient access capabilities for prescription management, portal password resets, and information assistance,” Alfonsi mentioned. “Our patients shouldn’t have to wait until business hours—or wait on hold—to manage routine tasks. Now they can verify once and take care of everyday needs in a single call, any time of day, and our team can focus on the conversations where a human touch matters most.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For 30 years, Thanksgiving has been a painful reminder for a Texas family whose holiday turned into a nightmare when their loved one was found strangled inside her Houston apartment.

Kristen Lea Wilson, 29, was preparing to spend Thanksgiving with her family in November 1996 when investigators say someone slipped into her first-floor apartment through a window, using a cat door to gain access, and waited for her to return home.

After cutting the telephone cord and unscrewing the lightbulbs to keep the apartment dark, the intruder waited in Wilson’s bedroom closet.

In a recent development, when she never highlighted up to Thanksgiving dinner the following day, her parents became worried and drove her apartment where they found her slain body. Three decades later, no one has been charged in her murder, and her family is still fighting for answers.

In a recent development, “Thirty years ago this Thanksgiving my sister Kristen Lea Wilson was murdered in Houston,” Kelly Wilson Hancock wrote in a recent social media post. “She was strangled–this was an up and personal murder. Her case has NEVER been solved.”.

Sources indicate that on Nov. 27, 1996, the day before Thanksgiving, Wilson stopped at a grocery store after work to pick up last-minute items for the family's holiday gathering at her grandparents' home in Katy, TX.

She returned to her apartment on Meadowglen Lane in southwest Houston, unloaded her groceries, and reportedly went into her bedroom to change clothes. Investigators believe her killer was already inside.

Recent findings suggest that according to the Houston Police Department, the intruder likely gained access by reaching through a cat door in the screen of a first-floor window and removing the window frame. Once inside, the killer allegedly cut the telephone cord and unscrewed lightbulbs, reportedly preparing to ambush Wilson in complete darkness.

According to recent reports, the apartment's accessibility became a crucial detail in the investigation, and raised troubling questions about security at the complex, especially because Wilson had allegedly expressed concerns about her safety before her death, her family mentioned. She had previously revealed an incident in which a maintenance worker allegedly entered her apartment without warning.

Recent findings suggest that when Wilson’s parents arrived at her apartment to check on her, they found the front door unlocked. Inside, Wilson's father made the horrific discovery–his daughter dead on the bedroom floor. She had been strangled and was partially undressed.

Police also noted a disturbing detail–her body appeared to have been deliberately positioned, with her ankles crossed and her hands resting in her lap.

In a recent development, investigators found evidence of a violent struggle, including broken fingernails, suggesting Wilson had fought desperately against her attacker. There were no reported witnesses to the killing, and surveillance cameras did not capture the suspect leaving the property.

Despite decades of investigation, extensive media coverage and advancements in forensic technologies, the identity of Wilson’s killer remains a mystery.

Three men associated with Wilson provided DNA samples to investigators shortly after her death, and each were ruled out as suspects based on the technology available at the time, according to an investigation by ABC13 Houston.

But Hancock believes mistakes made during the initial investigation have complicated efforts to solve her sister's murder.

It has been revealed that “From the get go, the detectives messed up,” she wrote in her recent post. “The original detective was going through a divorce and she wasn’t focused.”.

Recent findings suggest that she also expressed frustration over what she described as inconsistencies in the investigation. Investigators have since discovered that not all the evidence collected from the crime scene was tested, according to local reports.

Hancock said she has attempted to contact Othram, a forensic DNA laboratory that specializes in helping law enforcement investigate cold cases, about potentially examining evidence in her sister's murder.

“I’ve tried to reach out to Othram Labs to see if they can look at DNA, but the detective has to request it, from what I am told,” she wrote.

It is unclear whether Houston police have submitted evidence for additional testing or whether forensic genetic genealogy could be used in the case.

For the Wilson family, Thanksgiving had always been one of their favorite celebrations.

“Thanksgiving was the biggest event of the year,” Hancock told ABC13. “We’d all go over there, and it was just a massive family get-together. It was so much fun.”.

Industry observers note that wilson, described by her sister as independent and ambitious, had introduced a small business that provided office services to local companies. Wilson, the middle of three girls, was also devoted to her family, especially her young niece and nephew.

"She was like a second mother to my son and daughter,” Hancock mentioned. “She was just so beautiful with an infectious smile. My mom always called her the golden child because she just was. I hate to say she was perfect, but she pretty much was.”.

The Wilson family was devastated by her murder and to this day are still struggling with questions that remain unanswered three decades later.

Recent findings suggest that “My grandma used the words ‘brutally murdered.’ I’ll never forget the call telling me Kristen had been killed," Hancock said. "My whole world was… our whole family’s world was turned upside down. Personally, I think she knew the person, but I don’t know.".

Wilson's father, who discovered her body, has since passed away without learning who killed his daughter.

As the family marks the 30th anniversary of Wilson's death this Thanksgiving, her sister continues to push for answers.

Hancock noted Houston police Detective Richard Rodriguez, who previously discussed the case in ABC13's Unsolved series, is now handling the investigation. She is hoping that with fresh eyes on the case, renewed publicity and advances in forensic technology might finally produce a breakthrough.

But no matter how much time has passed, Wilson's sister said the anniversary is another reminder of the holidays, birthdays and other family events her sister has missed.

It has been revealed that “Hug your loved ones tight, you just never know," she wrote. "Miss my sister so much.".

Anyone with information about Wilson's murder is urged to contact the Houston Police Department or Crime Stoppers of Houston.

Millennials living in rural areas have 42% more documented chronic conditions on average compared to those in other environments, a fresh report from athenaInstitute found.

And, millennials in rural communities are 47% more likely to have at least two chronic conditions. This heavier chronic disease burden extends to other generations as well, analysts note.

Half of Baby Boomers (50.4%) in rural areas have three or more documented conditions, which the report notes is “on par” with non-rural individuals in the Silent and Greatest generations.

The 2026 Rural Ambulatory Care Report (PDF) analyzed athenahealth network data from 12.3 million rural patients between 2021 and 2025, along with more than 30,000 clinicians and 1,861 rural practices across the U.S. It examined factors such as appointment activity, workforce composition, payments, and more.

Athenahealth CMO and athenaInstitute co-chair Nele Jessel, M.D., stated in a statement the findings show that while rural practices are not “standing still in the face of enormous challenges,” there are “limits to how much more they can absorb as patient needs continue to grow.”.

Recent findings suggest that “They are adapting how they deliver care and finding ways to keep patients connected to the care they need,” Jessel said. “With renewed focus on rural healthcare, there is a real opportunity to build on what is working by investing in the workforce, technology and models of care that can help these practices continue serving the communities that depend on them.”.

Primary care physicians in rural areas have to wear multiple hats, as specialty care needs at practices are higher in rural communities.

Industry observers note that the report found that primary care handles 68.7% of visits involving anxiety or depression diagnoses versus 55.1% in non-rural areas. Moreover, 25% of rural patients with documented anxiety or depression had a substance use disorder—up from 19.8% in non-rural communities.

Data shows rural and non-rural healthcare practices collected roughly the same share of what they were owed by insurers in 2025, but analysts note a difference in patient balances.

Rural practices collected about $70 of every $100 owed, while non-rural practices collected about $78—which analysts say is about a 10% gap.

Recent findings suggest that another potential source of financial vulnerability for rural practices is Medicaid. Medicaid covered 27.5% of rural visits, which analysts note leaves these practices more exposed to eligibility changes set to begin in 2027.

For better mental health, how often you exercise may matter more than how hard

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (820 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • How often you exercise may matter more for your mental health than how hard you push yourself during a workout.
  • The research, published in the open access journal PLOS One, was conducted by Michael Grasdalsmoen of Western Norway University of Applied Sciences and his colleagues.
  • Depression, anxiety, and other common mental health conditions are among the leading causes of disability in young adults worldwide.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

How often you exercise may matter more for your mental health than how hard you push yourself during a workout. A large study of Norwegian college students found that those who exercised less frequently were more likely to experience depression and anxiety one year later. The findings suggest that maintaining a consistent exercise routine could be particularly important for supporting mental well-being.

The research, published in the open access journal PLOS One, was conducted by Michael Grasdalsmoen of Western Norway University of Applied Sciences and his colleagues. Their results point to the potential benefits of exercising regularly rather than focusing primarily on longer or more demanding workouts.

Why Exercise Habits Matter for Mental Health.

Depression, anxiety, and other common mental health conditions are among the leading causes of disability in young adults worldwide. The college years can be an especially challenging period as students adjust to new academic, social, and personal responsibilities. Identifying everyday behaviors that may help protect mental health is therefore an crucial research priority.

Industry observers note that although previous research has linked regular physical activity to better psychological well-being, many young adults remain physically inactive. Scientists have also had relatively limited evidence about how exercise habits relate to the development of mental health conditions over time, particularly when those conditions are evaluated using standardized diagnostic tools.

Industry observers note that to investigate this relationship, Grasdalsmoen and his team followed 10,460 full-time students enrolled in higher education in Norway. Participants ranged in age from 18 to 35.

Industry observers note that at the beginning of the study, students completed questionnaires describing their exercise habits, including how frequently they worked out, how strenuous their activities were, how long they exercised, and how many total hours they were active each week. One year later, they completed a self-administered diagnostic assessment designed to identify common mental health disorders.

Exercise Frequency May Matter More Than Intensity.

In a recent development, the researchers found that students who reported lower levels of physical activity were more likely to meet diagnostic criteria for anxiety or depression one year later. However, not every aspect of exercise revealed the same relationship with mental health.

Industry observers note that exercise frequency emerged as a particularly consistent factor. How often students exercised was more reliably associated with their later mental health than the intensity of their workouts or the amount of time they spent exercising.

The researchers also identified differences between men and women. Among women, lower exercise intensity was associated with a greater likelihood of anxiety and depression. Among men, spending fewer total hours exercising each week demonstrated a stronger association with these conditions.

Overall, the likelihood of common mental health disorders decreased as weekly exercise increased, with this pattern continuing up to approximately 10 hours of physical activity per week.

The results also support the World Health Organization's recommendation that adults complete at least 150 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity each week.

Regular Exercise Could Help Support Student Mental Health.

Sources indicate that taken together, the findings suggest that exercising consistently may be especially valuable for reducing the likelihood of anxiety and depression among college students. Rather than concentrating exclusively on workout intensity or duration, maintaining a regular routine could be an important part of supporting mental health.

However, the researchers emphasize that their observational study cannot establish a direct cause-and-effect relationship. Although students who exercised more regularly tended to have better mental health outcomes, the results do not prove that exercise itself prevented depression or anxiety.

Industry observers note that even with this limitation, promoting accessible opportunities for physical activity could be a useful part of broader efforts to improve student well-being. Such efforts may be especially relevant for students who are beginning to experience mental health difficulties or symptoms that have not yet reached the threshold for a clinical diagnosis.

The authors add: "Our findings show that students who engage in regular physical exercise are at lower risk of developing common mental disorders over time. These findings highlight the importance of making physical activity an accessible and natural part of student life.".

"Mental health among students is a growing public health concern. Our findings suggest that supporting students to be physically active may contribute to better mental health and should be recognized as an important part of a healthy learning environment.".

Funding: The SHoT study was financially supported by the Norwegian Ministry of Education and Research (2017) and the Norwegian Ministry of Health and Care Services (2016). Neither funding organization participated in designing the research, collecting or analyzing data, deciding whether to publish the findings, or preparing the manuscript.

UPDATED 17:27 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Shares of human resources and finance software firm Workday Inc. fell more than 7% in late trading today after a softer-than-expected subscription revenue forecast for the current quarter overshadowed fiscal third-quarter earnings and revenue that came in ahead of Wall Street’s targets.

In a recent development, for the quarter that ended on Oct. 31, Workday reported adjusted earnings per share of $2.82, up 22% from $2.32 in the same quarter of the previous year, on revenue of $2.705 billion, up 11.2% year-over-year. Analysts were expecting earnings of $2.75 per share on revenue of $2.69 billion.

Subscription revenue rose 12.8% from a year earlier, to $2.532 billion. Net income on an unadjusted basis came to $237 million, down from $252 million in the same quarter a year ago. Included in the quarter were $51 million in restructuring expenses, which followed the tech giant’s disclosure in late September that it would cut about 2.5% of its workforce, mostly in its product and technology team.

Total subscription revenue backlog grew 6.1%, to $27.548 billion, with the 12-month figure up 12.3%, to $9.216 billion. Free cash flow came to $691 million, up from $550 million. During the quarter, Workday spent $750 million buying back about 3.8 million shares.

Sources indicate that the quarter also saw Workday hold its annual Rising customer conference in Las Vegas in October, when the company made Sana the new home experience for its platform. Built on technology from Sana Labs AB, which Workday acquired for about $1.1 billion last year, Sana is an AI interface that brings tasks, decisions, meetings and agent activity together in one place. Autopilot Agents, also released at the event, are designed to handle routine HR, finance and IT processes in the background.

On the opening day of Rising, Workday unveiled that it had agreed to acquire agentic identity platform ConductorOne Inc., better known as C1.ai. That deal closed on Monday. A partnership with Anthropic PBC, also unveiled at Rising, is set to bring Claude together with Sana AI agents and Workday’s HR and finance data.

In a recent development, “The past few quarters have been our strongest on the innovation and invention front, and in Q3, our AI products drove nearly $150 million in newly introduced ACV, more than three times what we delivered a year ago,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Aneel Bhusri, who returned to the top job in February after Carl Eschenbach stepped down. The priority now, Bhusri added, is to get more customers running agents in production.

According to Workday, the number of core customers that have bought at least one of its AI products rose nearly 25% from the previous quarter, to more than 2,200.

Pointing to what he called “ongoing adoption across our AI portfolio,” Chief Financial Officer Zane Rowe remarked the tech giant is raising its full-year targets.

It has been revealed that for its fiscal fourth quarter, Workday expects subscription revenue of $2.6 billion, up 10%, and an adjusted operating margin of 31.7%. Full-year subscription revenue is now forecast at $9.958 billion, up 13%, compared with the $9.94 billion to $9.95 billion guided in August. The full-year adjusted operating margin forecast was also raised, to 31.5%, ahead of the 31.1% expected by analysts.

Though the full-year numbers moved higher, the fourth-quarter subscription forecast came in narrowly below the $2.61 billion analysts had been expecting. Growth of 10% in the period would also be a step down from the 12.8% Workday posted in the third quarter.

Having a solid digital marketing strategy is essential if you want to succeed as a business owner in the modern day. Effective digital marketing lets you get more eyes on your business and ensure consistent growth.

Because digital marketing trends are forever changing, it’s key to stay on top of your brand’s strategy. Doing so ensures that you stand out above your competitors and gain the recognition that your brand deserves.

It has been revealed that if you’re unsure how to master your digital marketing strategy, consider working with an expert company that can help you figure out which direction to go. A professional agency, such as Scorpion Digital Marketing Agency, can support your online efforts to maximize your success.

If you don’t want to outsource your digital marketing processes, try these top tips below to maintain an effective digital marketing strategy and boost your business growth.

Upgrade and Optimize Your Website.

Sources indicate that your website is where most of your fresh audience will find your business and your existing customers will shop for your new products and services. If you create a strong first impression through your website, you can gain credibility and authority in your industry.

Make sure to regularly update your website content so it’s accurate and on-trend. Doing so also signals to Google that your website is authoritative and credible, increasing your rankings on search engine results pages (SERPs).

The higher your rankings, the higher your visibility, meaning you can expand your reach with minimal effort. When updating your content, use plenty of industry-relevant keywords and key phrases to ensure your target audience finds your site.

With a strong social media strategy, you can significantly expand your reach and gain recognition as a trustworthy brand. Regularly posting content enables you to provide consistent value to your audience while displaying your expertise.

Recent findings suggest that you can create posts highlighting the benefits of your products or the quality of your services. You can share positive testimonials and reviews from happy customers to build your credibility.

Industry observers note that social media platforms allow you to connect directly with your target audience too. You can answer queries and concerns in your DMs and show the human side of your brand.

Whether you use live or pre-filmed video content, you can capture your target audience's attention and provide helpful information in an engaging way. You can share demonstrations of how to use your products or explain your services in more detail to persuade consumers to check out your brand.

Optimize your videos for search engines by including keywords and phrases in your video titles and descriptions. Doing so increases your rankings on SERPs and puts your brand in front of as many people as possible.

#169329. Keto diet slashes liver fat by 67% in just 4 months

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1200 w)
